title: Zoom in: validators pull only what they have credit for
caption: Free slots are the credit. A validator that is slow for any reason asks for less, and the log's lag carries that signal back to admission.

messages.label: fetch, credit 50
messages.note: The validator has 50 free slots, so it asks for exactly 50 batches. It never holds more than it can work on.

messages.label: check gaps, dupes
messages.note: Missing quarter-hours are flagged for estimation; a batch seen before is skipped.

messages.label: write 50 (idempotent)
messages.note: Key = meter id + interval, so writing the same read twice changes nothing.

messages.label: commit offset, credit 50
messages.note: Commit after the write: a crash means redelivery, never loss. Throughput = 50 slots ÷ 0.1 s ≈ 500 batches/s per validator.

messages.label: lag: 40 s
messages.note: Lag in seconds of work, not in messages, is what admission reacts to.

scenarios.name: Writes slow down
scenarios.summary: Slower writes mean slots stay busy; the validator simply stops asking, and the lag tells admission to push back.

messages.label: ok after 0.5 s
messages.note: Each slot is busy 5× longer: ~100 batches/s per validator instead of ~500.

messages.label: no free slots: no fetch
messages.note: Nothing piles up inside the validator; the backlog stays in the durable log.

messages.label: lag: 30 min
messages.note: Admission starts answering 429 to gateways for billing reads and drops diagnostics.

scenarios.name: Validator crashes
scenarios.summary: A crash between the write and the commit replays the batch; idempotent writes make the replay harmless.

messages.label: crash before commit
messages.note: The offset was never committed, so the log still owns all 50 batches.

messages.label: redeliver 50 to a new validator
messages.note: After the session timeout the partition moves to another validator.

messages.label: write 50 (idempotent)
messages.note: The 30 already written overwrite themselves with the same values: no double usage.

scenarios.name: Scale out on lag
scenarios.summary: Instead of pushing back, add validators: each new one brings 50 more credits, up to the number of log partitions.

messages.label: lag: 10 min
messages.note: Above the 5-minute target the autoscaler adds validators.

messages.label: start 10 more
messages.note: Startup takes a couple of minutes; the bound covers the gap.

messages.label: write (idempotent)
messages.note: The time-series DB is the next limit: more validators only help until it saturates.
